Sentence (English): I bought it and it sat in a box in my apartment for 6 months or so.
Comments (English): I bought it and it sat in a box in my apartment for 6 months or so. Installed it and immediately had problems with it running. I'd press start and it would just make a low rumbling noise and then time out. Got one wash out of it before I returned to just hand washing my dishes. Renovated my kitchen and had my guy reinstall it because maybe I had done something wrong. It ran twice after that and now I am having the same problems. The machine has ran 3 times since I've had it and has been nothing but problems. All 3 times I've ran it the water has not drained and left smelly dirty water in the bottom that I've had to take out with a cup and a towel.

Sentence (English): I did really like this dishwasher.
Comments (English): I did really like this dishwasher. It did a great job washing dishes, I like the third rack. I bought it through Costco so have the extra 2 year warranty. Well, the motor died at 2 years 4 months. Per the technician that came out to diagnose the problem, the said that the microfiltration system that the new dishwashers have, can get clogged and burn out the motor. There is no way to access the microfiltration to clean it yourself to prevent this from happening. Note taken when looking for a new dishwasher!

Sentence (English): I think the first most obvious reason that I love my washer is that it is so quiet.
Comments (English): [ Love my dishwasher! ] || ---------------- || I think the first most obvious reason that I love my washer is that it is so quiet. However there is of course much more. The built in water softener is a god send. So little effort to fill it but the impacts are noticeable. No film left after washing. Even if it was slight you'll notice a huge difference in the clarity of crystal/ glass. The extra third rack I am a bit mixed about. It's great for being organized and makes unloading flatware so much easier. However, I've found that the guides used to position the flatware can actually get in the way of cleaning. Take a spoon with pasta sauce that's sat in the dishwasher for a few days. There's a good chance that where the guide points are located theee may be some sauce that doesn't get washed away. I haven't had my washer long enough to know if that's a frequent issue. So far it's not but it has happened on a couple of loads. I guess one could contrast this with the standard flatware bin which is anyone's bet. The top rack spaces out the flatware appropriately and allows you to keep like with like (forks with forks) so at unloading time you can literally sweep them all up and they are ready for the drawer.

Comments (English): [ 3 types of magic, 3 types of slave, buy without hesitation. ] || ---------------- || I used to put off washing dishes because I didn't want to bother with them, and then I would often do them in a hurry the next morning. But after I put the dishwasher in, the dishes stopped piling up in the sink. If the No. 1 Slave dryer was very satisfying with just the fluffy towels, and the No. 2 Slave robot vacuum cleaner gave me an hour-long walk every day, the No. 3 Slave dishwasher saved my back that was suffering because of the low sink height. Sentence (English): I have always thought the dishwasher commercials showing people putting barely dirty dishes or a like a like cake into the dishwasher were so stupid.
Comments (English): [ The most Adultiest Rave review of a dishwasher ] || ---------------- || I have always thought the dishwasher commercials showing people putting barely dirty dishes or a like a like cake into the dishwasher were so stupid. It would never get stuff clean. I grew up with a dishwasher and have had one in my home my entire life. I have NEVER been able to put a mostly dirty dish in there with the hopes that it would come out clean. Dishwashers were more for sanitizing the dishes after a mostly hand wash. This LG QuadWash dishwasher is NOT the dishwasher of ages past but what dreams are made of. I don't always like to do the dinner dishes at night, sometimes they get done in the morning. I decided to take this baby for a spin and see what it could do. Comments (English): [ Adequate for the price ] || ---------------- || This is an entry level dishwasher, bought at Costco because the price included delivery, installation, and removal of the old appliance. Elsewhere it would be several hundred dollars less without delivery and installation. Its performance is adequate - I see no food left on dishes after even the short one-hour cycle. You get what you pay for - the interior is plastic, not stainless steel as on higher priced models, it is noticeably noisey compared to more expensive models, has only a basic silverware rack (no covered area for small objects, no flip-up cover with individual utensil slots), the non-adjustable upper rack has no secondary side rack for stacking short glasses/cups, no bottle-jet as on higher end models, just a few cycle choices, the main pull out rack is not well-guided and frequently mistracks when you put it in or out. It's basic but serviceable. I've had no problems in several months of use. It's a low end model so keep your expectations down and it will be fine. Longevity remains to be determined.

We haven't noticed a major difference between using heavy, sani, dry boost - all the full power settings turned on - except that it takes a couple hours longer, so we've settled on mainly using the normal cycle setting. We've only had the dishwasher for 3 weeks, so we'll see how it holds up.

Comments (English): [ BOSCH 500 Series dishwasher ] || ---------------- || I'm returning this dishwasher. It didn't work for me from the get-go. The printed instructions are completely inadequate. I shouldn't have to rely on a phone app to get it to work. Every time I used this dishwasher it stopped before the cycle was finished and the beeper blared until I opened the door. Sometimes food was still stuck to the utensils. A Bosch repairman came to try to help me out and even he had problems figuring out how to work this machine. It's just not intuitive. He called it "a frikkin design"!

With this in mind, I rarely put things on the 3rd upper rack, which was a feature I thought I'd really like, since my old one didn't have that. Overall it gets the job done, and still better than most other brands, but not nearly as great as our old one.

Sentence (English): We've had marginal experience with dishwashers over the years, with the predecessor of this Bosch 800 series dishwasher being rendered useless after a critical part had been discontinued.
Comments (English): [ A dishwasher that actually washes dishes! ] || ---------------- || We've had marginal experience with dishwashers over the years, with the predecessor of this Bosch 800 series dishwasher being rendered useless after a critical part had been discontinued. We settled on the Bosch 800 series after doing a lot of research, because we did not want to get stuck with another mediocre dishwasher. So far we have not needed to rewash anything that we've put into this dishwasher, and have been extremely happy with the features and operation of it. By the way, it is VERY quiet which has made the lack of a delayed start not a big deal. Sentence (English): (This review was collected as part of a promotion.)
Comments (English): [ Love my dishwasher! ] || ---------------- || (This review was collected as part of a promotion.) I think the first most obvious reason that I love my washer is that it is so quiet. However there is of course much more. The built in water softener is a god send. So little effort to fill it but the impacts are noticeable. No film left after washing. Even if it was slight you'll notice a huge difference in the clarity of crystal/ glass. The extra third rack I am a bit mixed about. It's great for being organized and makes unloading flatware so much easier. However, I've found that the guides used to position the flatware can actually get in the way of cleaning. Take a spoon with pasta sauce that's sat in the dishwasher for a few days. There's a good chance that where the guide points are located theee may be some sauce that doesn't get washed away. I haven't had my washer long enough to know if that's a frequent issue. So far it's not but it has happened on a couple of loads. I guess one could contrast this with the standard flatware bin which is anyone's bet. The top rack spaces out the flatware appropriately and allows you to keep like with like (forks with forks) so at unloading time you can literally sweep them all up and they are ready for the drawer.

Sentence (English): Unfortuntately, it has been nearly 3 weeks and we have yet been able to run our first cycle with our new dishwasher, At this point (2/7), I have yet to hear recent feedback from Whirlpool on the status of my situation.
Comments (English): [ Unresolved prolonged issue w/ defective dishwasher ] || ---------------- || Unfortuntately, it has been nearly 3 weeks and we have yet been able to run our first cycle with our new dishwasher, At this point (2/7), I have yet to hear recent feedback from Whirlpool on the status of my situation. In summary, here is the timeline of events:1/21 Purchased d/w at Lowe's1/23 D/W delivered to our home.1/27 Installed d/w. Identified a leak in bottom left at corner of basin.1/29 Visited Lowe's to request an exchange for a functioning dishwasher. They said they couldn't do that and I had to call Whirlpool. 1/29 I called Whirlpool customer service line. They said I had to have their service tech review the appliance. Soonest appointment was 2/2.2/2 VIA service tech diagnosed that the problem was a defective appliance. The basin was cracked at the bottom left seam of the basin. They said that they would need to order a new basin, disassemble, and rebuild the d/w, which is now no longer a new d/w but a refurbished one. Plus the basin is not in stock and still as of today on backorder. Not satisfied with this resolution.2/3 Visted Lowe's and discussed with several managers a request for an exchange. They asked if I had a Return Authorization (RA) number from Whirlpool. I said no. They provided me the phone number to call Whirlpool to request an RA number. (Had to wait until Monday to call.)2/5 Called Whirlpool (talked with Paige). They said that they do not provide RA numbers to customers. I would need Lowes to request an RA number.2/5 Returned to Lowes to ask them to request Whirlpool provide an RA number. Whirlpool did not provide. They did send an email to me stating that if I provided the receipt, they would work to provide an exchange.2/5 I immediately emailed my receipt.2/7 I have received no communication as to the status or confirmation of the remedy for my situation.I am disheartened by both Lowes and Whirlpool for their inability to empower employees to make reasonable decisions on situations. I understand the need for some rigidity in the policies since I'm sure customers take advantage of return policies. Sentence (English): I've been using Bespoke for about a year, and even when I dry it with hot air, some moisture remains and there's a lot of water on the heel, so I turn it over to remove it.
Comments (English): I've been using Bespoke for about a year, and even when I dry it with hot air, some moisture remains and there's a lot of water on the heel, so I turn it over to remove it. I use it because my joints hurt, but to save electricity, I don't use hot air drying, and when I'm done, I just turn it over to remove the accumulated water on the heel and place it face down again, and it dries quickly. However, before that, instead of drying well, the fan that removes water vapor ran vigorously and spewed out a large amount of water vapor. This is noisy, but running the motor a lot also consumes a lot of electricity. The new products seem to consume less electricity as they open automatically and dry naturally rather than using electricity.

It seems to perform its task adequately, at least for the first month of operation, but the overall quality of the physical material is reminiscent of a bargain basement dealer.

Sentence (English): This dishwasher seems to be very good so far.
Comments (English): [ Dishwasher is great, installation not so much.  ] || ---------------- || This dishwasher seems to be very good so far. It cleans and dries well, and is quiet. I am including some info for others that I learned through this purchase. First, be aware that "free installation" may not actually be free. Most states now require dishwashers to have a plug installed under your sink to plug into. Also, in my state I was required to have a water hammer aggressor on the lines. Before letting me make an appointment, my installer made me sign an agreement saying if I don't have these two things installed that they would do it for a charge of $400. I took care of it myself for much less money. I'd advise looking into these things and being aware of this when purchasing any dishwasher. Second, if you live in a cold climate, don't let the delivery leave the dishwasher in a garage. I had a week span between delivery and install and the water in the lines (they are tested at the factory) froze and the dishwasher would not work initially. The installer said I was his second costco dishwasher install that day that was frozen. Lastly, its worth mentioning that there seems to be a disconnect between Costco and the Installer. Delivery and installation are done by two different companies. Delivery for us was good, but install was a bit of a nightmare. There was literally zero communication from the installer and they would not answer their phone. Both Costco and I tried numerous times to reach the installer without success. I was given an install date and time by Costco which they claim was provided by the installer but nobody showed up that day. The installer eventually told me they did not give this info to Costco. After a huge struggle, I finally got an install appointment. The installer showed up 2 hours after the time slot and the install was not done very well (I was able to correct the issues with this myself). Some advice to others is to not rely on the install info that Costco has. Overall this was a pretty stressful purchase, but the dishwasher is great.

Sentence (English): I purchased my KitchenAid dishwasher in April of 2021.
Comments (English): [ Very Disappointed ] || ---------------- || I purchased my KitchenAid dishwasher in April of 2021. We are empty nesters and rarely used this machine but would use it if we hosted a party. probably used it a dozen times or less. Although I don't feel the machine cleaned cooking vessels especially well, I honestly didn't expect it to, it cleaned most dishes and cutlery just fine. I'm not talking about baked on food or heavy deposits. just normal food deposits. I attempted to use the machine last week, loaded my dishes and cutlery and turned it on. The cycle was completed when I checked the next morning but found that the dishes were still dirty so I checked to see if there was anything blocking the arms from rotating, (I know the hot water was loaded and drained), and the soap was dispensed properly. there were no obstructions so I loaded more detergent and put it through another cycle. Same result. It seems that the washer arms were not functioning so the machine was simply filling up and emptying. Unfortunately I have passed the 2 year warranty period so no relief from Costco, so now I need to decide whether I invest more money in this machine via repairs knowing it doesn't hold up or purchase a different branded machine, probably a Maytag from Costco. It really stinks that an item I purchased malfunctioned so quickly after so little use. My problem is not with Costco but I would stay away from KitchenAid products. They're not what they used to be.

Sentence (English): It really does clean dishes that haven't been pre-rinsed.
Comments (English): [ So Glad to Have A Bosch Dishwasher! ] || ---------------- || It really does clean dishes that haven't been pre-rinsed. I love the third top drawer utinsel holder. Having trouble adjustiing to new spaces on the middle drawer, but all-in-all the racks hold enough for a large dinner party. I think it's weird I have to go onto my phone if I want the delicate dish cycle--whoever decided that wasn't a high enough priority for just having a button on the washer itself? I bought online from Appliance.com and installation was supposed to be included but the delivery guys said they couldn't do it and then the appliance repair guy I hired didn't do it correctly. The washer kept insisting the door was open when it wasn't. I finally called the Bosch people and they sent an authorized Bosch guy--I waited a week. The little clips that hold the dishwasher from falling forward had not been included with the machine. Luckily he had them onthe truck. If I had know I could get a Bosch repairman in to install, I would have been so happy. Four instead of five stars because delicate cycle can only be assessed online and problems with installation.

Sentence (English): We purchased the Bosch as a replacement to 22-year-old Sears dishwasher, and choose Bosch based on Consumer Reports ratings.
Comments (English): [ Quiet dishwasher ] || ---------------- || We purchased the Bosch as a replacement to 22-year-old Sears dishwasher, and choose Bosch based on Consumer Reports ratings. Important to know when selecting Bosch dishwashers, they are plug in only, they are not hardwired. This means you will need to add an electrical outlet receptacle, either in a wall at the back of the dishwasher, or adjacent cabinet if possible. If you require a hardwired connection, make sure you purchase Bosch accessory kit SMZPCJB1UC. Also be aware that all connections, i.e., electrical, water supply and drain line take place at the rear of the unit and not underneath the unit. If this is a replacement dishwasher, you may have to relocate those lines. The unit cleans dishes and silverware very well, drying is good, and has multiple adjustable tines and racks. The dishwasher is also very quiet, so much so we have found ourselves checking it to make sure we turned it on.

Sentence (English): I had a series 100 dishwasher that lasted 18 years without being serviced(beyond cleaning).
Comments (English): [ Once again using Bosch .  ] || ---------------- || I had a series 100 dishwasher that lasted 18 years without being serviced(beyond cleaning). I got another year after changing the water inlet valve that had become inoperable from our terrible water. It was time to let it go when the racks were rusting through and an electrical problem had developed. I tried to replace it with a Bosch but due to availability problems from the Covid pandemic, there were none available. I ended up getting a comparable model from another maker (and what a mistake that was; life was not good). The Non-Bosch replacement developed electrical problems and the once quiet motor became very loud . and this was after 18 months of use. Of course it was out of warranty and getting it serviced would take me half way to a new one so, what to do? I got another Bosch. This was easier to set up than my prior Bosch Dishwasher as it came with a cord that I didn't have to hardwire. Is this quiet? You bet! Not only that, it is remotely controlable (if you are in to that kind of thing . you can still operate it from the front control panel). It does an excellent job on the dishes, and is quiet, which is important as we run it at night. This was not the cheapest, nor was the most expensive dishwasher available but for it's price and features, I think it represents an excellent value. Will it last 20 years? I have no way of knowing for sure but I expect it will.

Sentence (English): I did a lot of planning for a dishwasher.
Comments (English): I did a lot of planning for a dishwasher. Just because the cabinet is one centimeter shorter, there are fewer options. Most brands of dishwashers are above 770mm. Only Haier dishwashers can control the height within 760mm. , so I chose among Haier products and saw that the pressure of this model reached 50,000 Pa, and the color was relatively close to my cabinets, so I made a decisive move. As soon as the goods arrived, we started to install them immediately. During the previous decoration, water, electricity and sewage outlets were reserved, so the entire installation process was completed in more than ten minutes. I tried washing the dishes once. The machine is very good and the sound is not loud. During the drying process, the door will automatically open to dry the water vapor, and then it will automatically close the door. It is a perfect cupboard.
Comments (Original): 为了一台洗碗机，做了很多攻略，就因为橱柜做矮了一公分，少了很多选择，大部分牌子的洗碗机都在770mm以上，只有海尔洗碗机高度尺寸能控制在760以内，所以在海尔的产品中选择，看到这款压力达到了50000帕，而且颜色也和我家的橱柜比较接近，就果断出手了。一到货就马上动手安装好，之前装修时水电、排污口都预留了，所以整个安装过程十多分钟就搞定了。试着洗了一次碗，机器很不错，声音不大，烘干过程会自动打开门晾干水汽，之后会自动把门关上，就是一个完美的碗柜了。

Sentence (English): I love my new dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Love my new dishwasher! ] || ---------------- || I love my new dishwasher. It's quiet and to my surprise it dries the dishes really well (not even puddles on the bottom of the coffee cups). I honestly did not expect this. I know from experience that the high efficiency dishwashers don't seem to dry very well. Everyone I know that has one says they open their dishwasher up after it runs to let everything air dry. Well, great, but you shouldn't have to do that unless you want to. I also love the 3rd rack for small utensils, lids, etc. I went with the Cafe line because I loved the design aesthetic and they had decent reviews. This dishwasher is beautiful. I hope it stands the test of time. It replaced a 16 year old unit (not GE) that worked fine but sounded like a locomotive. If I had one criticism it would be the cycle time - it takes forever. But I think that is the norm for units these days. I'm happy.

Sentence (English): Like many, I did a lot of Internet research before buying this.
Comments (English): [ Net positive with some quirks. ] || ---------------- || Like many, I did a lot of Internet research before buying this. The one thing that doesn't prepare you for is the layout of the rack, because the pictures never show it from enough angles to get the full sense of it. Coming from a Maytag, which had a more straightforward boxy, gridded layout, I had a very hard time trying to understand what the designers were going for with this multi-angled bottom and a tine pattern that seemed like it was trying to shoehorn me into putting plates or bowls on the upper rack, which is not how I roll. It was so bad for us that I almost returned the dishwasher strictly because of the racks. Another issue is the leveling feet never quite worked right. No matter how many times I turn the middle screw which raises or lowers the back foot, I can't raise it enough, and the racks always slide closed on us while we are loading. That is a major annoyance. I can't lower the front any more because the front braces will rip out of the counter top if it goes any lower in front. So either my floors are sloping toward the walls (which is not how sagging floors generally work), or we have some leveling design issues here with the unit. It's also slightly noisier than the previous dishwasher, but, not to the point where I consider it a problem. However, the dishes were getting so clean! So, I resisted the urge to return it, and decided to just try to adapt the way I load it to what this unit needed. I'm still only about to fit about 80% of the dishes that we used to be able to load in the old one, but, I'm getting used to the different approach and different rhythm of this model. It's getting the dishes super clean, 3 months into the installation, and that's really what counts the most, in the end. I'm not saying I'd definitely buy this one again, but I wouldn't rule it out either. We'll see how well it holds up before I make that call.

So either my floors are sloping toward the walls (which is not how sagging floors generally work), or we have some leveling design issues here with the unit.It's also slightly noisier than the previous dishwasher, but, not to the point where I consider it a problem.However, the dishes were getting so clean!  So, I resisted the urge to return it, and decided to just try to adapt the way I load it to what this unit needed.  I'm still only about to fit about 80% of the dishes that we used to be able to load in the old one, but, I'm getting used to the different approach and different rhythm of this model.  It's getting the dishes super clean, 3 months into the installation, and that's really what counts the most, in the end.I'm not saying I'd definitely buy this one again, but I wouldn't rule it out either.  We'll see how well it holds up before I make that call.

This is my fault for only going for what was on sale. I would have gotten a larger capacity, more featured unit. It is fine for a rental or small family, but I was expecting more from a baseline Bosch. My model doesn't have adjustable racks and some of the download programs suggested and downloaded are not available to use. Bosch should be able to taylor download features to those that are available on a particular machine.With that being said, this unit cleans and sanitizes very well. I like the wifi connection for starting and seeing how much longer remains on the cycle. Would I buy a Bosch again, certainly. However I would like one with more room inside, have adjustable racks, and make sure it has the advanced cycles available I am expecting. I know those models are available and I will do my homework in the future.

Sentence (English): I think it's worth the price.
Comments (English): [ It's a revolution to get away from washing dishes! But ] || ---------------- || I think it's worth the price. The installer was friendly and there were no problems. It's in Jeju Island. First of all, the installer told me to only use an all-in-one solid detergent that contains both rinse and detergent. There is a rinse container, but I don't know why it says to only use all-in-one solid detergent. The biggest problem with this product is that you put all-in-one detergent in the detergent container, close it, and run the dishwasher. Out of 5 runs, the detergent doesn't dissolve 3 times and stays stuck to the detergent box. Since we are a two-person household, we don't do a lot of dishes, so we cut it in half and use it, but this bothers me a little. The detergent isn't completely dissolved (it feels like a little powder), but it looks like it was washed to some extent. However, it feels dirty, so I run it once more. P2 is the basic mode, but if you use another mode, out of 10, the detergent doesn't dissolve at all. The basic mode seems to have the best cleaning power. Even if you run it for a longer time than the basic mode, the cleaning power isn't as good as the basic mode. In the P2 basic mode, the detergent dissolves properly 2 out of 5 times, so I don't use the other modes. Even things like meat grease are clean after running it twice. And the mesh in the drain part? It can be separated from the machine, but no matter what I do, it won't separate after I take it out. According to the manual, it seems to be separated, but mine doesn't. But it's not so bad that I can't wash it, so I'll just keep using it. But! The fact that it's almost half the price compared to other products is a huge merit. If you're stressed out from washing dishes in a household of 1-2 people, I recommend it. Just turn it twice. If your partner is good at Tetris, they'll like it if you give them lots of praise. It seems like they're having fun later on. Just being freed from washing dishes like this is very satisfying. Again fairly simple straightforward There's only three real connections you're worried about the main water source the power of course and then the drain tube. Sentence (English): The three levels of shelving are very convenient, as is the ability to adjust the height of the middle shelf.
Comments (English): [ Very Quiet ] || ---------------- || The three levels of shelving are very convenient, as is the ability to adjust the height of the middle shelf. There are lots of options for adjusting levers in each shelf to organize, but I don't understand why there are added levers for cups. They don't lay flat and I'm not sure that two layers of cups would get clean, nor would the second layer be well supported. Maybe it would help with bottles and other unusual items. The same part can support a wine glass handle, which again, I couldn't make work with mine. That is in the back corners of the middle rack. I will probably remove them for good. The part I wish provided more support was the horizontal middle of the bottom rack. It feels an awkward distance between the two rows is left in the middle, only usable for a few bigger bowls, like small serving size. I'd rather have this space left to each edge rather than the middle. So far what I have is either too big or too small for that spot. Some things would go nicely there, but only if there were enough plates to support them. Maybe my plates are just odd sized? The sound insulation is great, but the problem is the directions for installing it are not. The plumber and handyman gave up. My husband had to cut ours to get it installed without it interfering with the door being able to open all the way. That reduced the amazing sound insulation, unfortunately. It is still much quieter than my previous "quiet" one. There is a video on Youtube provided by the company and another video by someone installing his own who stumbled on the correct way to install it. I was trying to find that before my husband cut ours. I wasn't fast enough. Now for the one big disappointment, which is a pretty big deal. The bottom rack should have the wheels about a half inch wider so the rack doesn't slip off the grid and clang the dishes around and need realigned every single time we push it back in. We've only had it a week and that is already a pain. It seems like a design flaw or a production flaw. It also slides back inside too fast to use unless it is all the way out. It is advertised as a washer that can be run when part full, but I haven't figured out all those types of things yet. One thing to note, the directions say it's best not to use the detergent pods for the types of cycles I would be running most. I have run three cycles and one of the three cycles didn't dissolve the pod and therefor only used half the detergent. Maybe I put it in the wrong spot. Last, the directions say I should be cleaning the filter monthly and that I may need to unclog some of the sprayer holes with a pin. I've never had to do that before and hope that is precautionary. I only had to clean my previous dishwashers filter a couple times, and never had to clean any of them with a toothbrush as the directions indicate. But maybe I never read the cleaning directions before either. I do appreciate the idea of the way this washer dries dishes with less energy. I love the sleek front and it seems the finish is truly finger print resistant. Unlike my refrigerator (another brand) that claimed it was. I'll be calling LG to see if my bottom washer rack falling off the tracks is a fluke. If one set of wheels is on, the set on the opposite side is on the verge of falling off. You only have 48 hours to check for flaws, which in my area was useless because the installer didn't come until a week after delivery. You would think Home Depot could coordinate drop off and hook up better. We had a really bad experience with both the delivery and the installation crews. Home Depot made it right in the end, but it was an extremely aggravating two weeks.

They don't lay flat and I'm not sure that two layers of cups would get clean, nor would the second layer be well supported. Maybe it would help with bottles and other unusual items. The same part can support a wine glass handle, which again, I couldn't make work with mine. That is in the back corners of the middle rack. I will probably remove them for good. The part I wish provided more support was the horizontal middle of the bottom rack. It feels an awkward distance between the two rows is left in the middle, only usable for a few bigger bowls, like small serving size. I'd rather have this space left to each edge rather than the middle. So far what I have is either too big or too small for that spot. Some things would go nicely there, but only if there were enough plates to support them. Maybe my plates are just odd sized? The sound insulation is great, but the problem is the directions for installing it are not. The plumber and handyman gave up. My husband had to cut ours to get it installed without it interfering with the door being able to open all the way. That reduced the amazing sound insulation, unfortunately. It is still much quieter than my previous "quiet" one. There is a video on Youtube provided by the company and another video by someone installing his own who stumbled on the correct way to install it. I was trying to find that before my husband cut ours. I wasn't fast enough. Now for the one big disappointment, which is a pretty big deal. The bottom rack should have the wheels about a half inch wider so the rack doesn't slip off the grid and clang the dishes around and need realigned every single time we push it back in. We've only had it a week and that is already a pain. It seems like a design flaw or a production flaw. It also slides back inside too fast to use unless it is all the way out. It is advertised as a washer that can be run when part full, but I haven't figured out all those types of things yet. One thing to note, the directions say it's best not to use the detergent pods for the types of cycles I would be running most. Last, the directions say I should be cleaning the filter monthly and that I may need to unclog some of the sprayer holes with a pin. I've never had to do that before and hope that is precautionary. I only had to clean my previous dishwashers filter a couple times, and never had to clean any of them with a toothbrush as the directions indicate. But maybe I never read the cleaning directions before either. I do appreciate the idea of the way this washer dries dishes with less energy. I love the sleek front and it seems the finish is truly finger print resistant. Unlike my refrigerator (another brand) that claimed it was. I'll be calling LG to see if my bottom washer rack falling off the tracks is a fluke. If one set of wheels is on, the set on the opposite side is on the verge of falling off. You only have 48 hours to check for flaws, which in my area was useless because the installer didn't come until a week after delivery. This is my fault for only going for what was on sale. I would have gotten a larger capacity, more featured unit. It is fine for a rental or small family, but I was expecting more from a baseline Bosch. My model doesn't have adjustable racks and some of the download programs suggested and downloaded are not available to use. Bosch should be able to taylor download features to those that are available on a particular machine. With that being said, this unit cleans and sanitizes very well. I like the wifi connection for starting and seeing how much longer remains on the cycle. Would I buy a Bosch again, certainly. However I would like one with more room inside, have adjustable racks, and make sure it has the advanced cycles available I am expecting. I know those models are available and I will do my homework in the future.

The box itself was flawless and undamaged. The installer and I attempted to bend the frame straight (like I said the frame can easily be bent with fingers like a paperclip) but realized this is stupid - I paid for a new dishwasher in working condition and shouldn't have to repair a brand new dishwasher. Either that or LG really skipped on the quality of this dishwasher. Just in case we're going to try a different brand. FYI if you're sent a damaged appliance from Costco they'll call you to confirm it's damaged that same day. However, to get a replacement you have to wait for a couple days for the Costco “resolution team” to call you and then begin the wait for your new dishwasher to come and try again. Overall not a great process.

Sentence (English): Had delivered by Lowes but installed by non-Loqes contractor since we had some repair work needed from an old leak.
Comments (English): [ Very happy ] || ---------------- || Had delivered by Lowes but installed by non-Loqes contractor since we had some repair work needed from an old leak. Was very nervous since installation was after the ridiculous 48hr return window, and it appeared we likely received a used machine (there was light mildew in some areas inside the machine and the filter had a long hair and some mildew, too). Ran a dishwasher cleaner through before using with dishes and had no issues. Have used it several times since and works great (normal wash only with 1 level of heated dry). Followed directions and put the dishwasher tab on the top rack - not in the container - to ensure it fully dissolves. A drying agent is a must to get the dishes dry, but that's expected. Some water is left in the lips of plastic containers and such but it's minimal. The silverware holder likes to catch on the rubber gasket when sliding the bottom rack in, but if you're careful with it it doesn't do that.

Sentence (English): I bought this product a little over a year ago and it has had a major component fail already.
Comments (English): [ Component flaw ] || ---------------- || I bought this product a little over a year ago and it has had a major component fail already. When the dishwasher was about a year old I noticed that some of the LED's on the clock display weren't working. Then occasionally the dishwasher would beep and lights flash during a cycle. I did an Online Chat with LG and included a video of what the dishwasher was doing. I was told that the beeping and flashing meant I needed to add a Rinse agent. As time went on the dishwasher started having more issues with the control panel. Randomly all the lights on the control panel would start flashing and at times it was difficult to turn off the control panel. This started happening more and more often. I again contacted LG and sent video's of the issue. The agent told me that resetting the dishwasher would correct the issue. I did that but still had LED lights out on the control panel and the dishwasher still randomly had lights flashing and at times when I turned it off it would come back on. I was given the name of a local certified LG service company to call. I called the company and paid them $150.00 to come out to look at the machine. Sentence (English): This is my 2nd Whirlpool dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ This dishy is a workhorse! ] || ---------------- || This is my 2nd Whirlpool dishwasher. The first one lasted over 10 years of fairly heavy use so I was willing to stick with the brand. I wanted a 3 rack design with minimal settings. This one is working very well. I do NOT use the detergent pods, I use the old fashioned loose, dry powder, with no rinse agent. I also don't rinse the dishes (I'll scrape off large chunks, but the small ones i expect the dishwasher to handle), and dishes may sit in the dishwasher for 3 days before the dishwasher gets run. We do have soft water. I do not use the dry cycle at all.Dishes have come out completely clean. If I'm home when the cycle is over, I'll open the door to allow air drying. If I run it before bed, dishes will be dry when I open the dishwasher in the morning. Yes, some of the plasticware may still be a bit wet, but are easily dried with a tea towel as they're being put away.The dishwasher is remarkably quiet. I like that you can see a countdown timer so you know how long is left. The 3rd rack really creates a lot more room. Because the layout of this dishwasher is simular to the old one, i can load it efficiently.If you want a workhorse dishwasher without a million bells and whistles that you'll never use, I definitely recommend this Whirlpool product.

Unless the item you are adding is very thin, the slots just are too close together. We have young kids in the house and use a lot of bowls and partitioned thick plastic plates, and they just do not sit in the slots well. Also, pots and pans do not seat well. The contractor they used locally to deliver and install delivered the dishwasher 2 days late and did not communicate with us at all that they would be delayed. After several attempts to contact them via phone and email (with no replies), I contacted Costco customer service. And while polite and showing concern, they were also unable to reach the provider. They created a case number and told me they would follow up, but never did. Overall, this was not only a underwhelming experience for the purchase, but the dishwasher is simply a poor design (racks only) and I feel like I have wasted $1300.

Sentence (English): This DW was a hurried choice b/c my 1st choice was too tall due to the addition of a tile floor in my kitchen - so immediate need for 32" height.
Comments (English): [ Very few Pros; multiple Cons ] || ---------------- || This DW was a hurried choice b/c my 1st choice was too tall due to the addition of a tile floor in my kitchen - so immediate need for 32" height. My bad - I rushed & didn't do my research. altho what bothers me may not have come up then. Comparison to an 18 yr old Frigidaire DW.Interior space not as big; top rack is not adjustable height wise, so limiting. Bottom rack variance in spoke heights VERY limiting to size of dishes, etc. that can be loaded - the same is true for the top rack - my 9 oz glassware falls over all the time & limited space for glassware below b/c of limited spoke size. No visual indicator either on the front or the top control panel when the cycle is complete. Smaller silverware caddy & the handle pulls off if the caddy load is full. Not broken; just pulls off, so not securely attached. I truly dislike the whole "condensation drying" method. I had never encountered it before now & definitely won't buy it again. More dampness & water leftover than a standard dryer method. Plus - price value not there. Was $200 more than the mid-range GE Profile 33.5" that I had selected but didn't fit. Minimal cycle options - DEFINITELY fewer than on my old model. Pros: It fit the space. Top of door controls. It is Quiet (important as my floor plan is open).Too expensive for me to replace very soon, but I'll be saving & researching for a replacement w/in the next couple of years.

Sentence (English): (This review was collected as part of a promotion.)
Comments (English): [ This dishy is a workhorse! ] || ---------------- || (This review was collected as part of a promotion.) This is my 2nd Whirlpool dishwasher. The first one lasted over 10 years of fairly heavy use so I was willing to stick with the brand. I wanted a 3 rack design with minimal settings. This one is working very well. I do NOT use the detergent pods, I use the old fashioned loose, dry powder, with no rinse agent. I also don't rinse the dishes (I'll scrape off large chunks, but the small ones i expect the dishwasher to handle), and dishes may sit in the dishwasher for 3 days before the dishwasher gets run. We do have soft water. I do not use the dry cycle at all.Dishes have come out completely clean. If I'm home when the cycle is over, I'll open the door to allow air drying. If I run it before bed, dishes will be dry when I open the dishwasher in the morning. Yes, some of the plasticware may still be a bit wet, but are easily dried with a tea towel as they're being put away.The dishwasher is remarkably quiet. I like that you can see a countdown timer so you know how long is left. The 3rd rack really creates a lot more room. Because the layout of this dishwasher is simular to the old one, i can load it efficiently.If you want a workhorse dishwasher without a million bells and whistles that you'll never use, I definitely recommend this Whirlpool product.

Sentence (English): This DW was a hurried choice b/c my 1st choice was too tall due to the addition of a tile floor in my kitchen - so immediate need for 32" height.
Comments (English): [ Very few Pros; multiple Cons ] || ---------------- || This DW was a hurried choice b/c my 1st choice was too tall due to the addition of a tile floor in my kitchen - so immediate need for 32" height. My bad - I rushed & didn't do my research. altho what bothers me may not have come up then. Comparison to an 18 yr old Frigidaire DW. Interior space not as big; top rack is not adjustable height wise, so limiting. Bottom rack variance in spoke heights VERY limiting to size of dishes, etc. that can be loaded - the same is true for the top rack - my 9 oz glassware falls over all the time & limited space for glassware below b/c of limited spoke size. No visual indicator either on the front or the top control panel when the cycle is complete. Smaller silverware caddy & the handle pulls off if the caddy load is full. Not broken; just pulls off, so not securely attached. I truly dislike the whole "condensation drying" method. I had never encountered it before now & definitely won't buy it again. More dampness & water leftover than a standard dryer method. Plus - price value not there. Was $200 more than the mid-range GE Profile 33.5" that I had selected but didn't fit. Minimal cycle options - DEFINITELY fewer than on my old model. Pros: It fit the space. Top of door controls. It is Quiet (important as my floor plan is open). Too expensive for me to replace very soon, but I'll be saving & researching for a replacement w/in the next couple of years.

I like the easily removable filter feature though the plastic seems cheep. Overall, I'm not satisfied. Sentence (English): I bought a Bosch because all the reviews said it was the best.
Comments (English): [ Quiet, nice looking, that's about it! ] || ---------------- || I bought a Bosch because all the reviews said it was the best. It is very quiet compared to our nearly 30 year old Maytag that finally gave out, but, and for me it's a very large but, it does not dry the dishes anywhere near as well! If you have anything that holds water it will be full when the dishes are done. Mainly this is a problem with plastic storage containers, they need to be placed completely upside down, and the lids need to be verticle. While I thought the upper rack would be really nice for silverware, spoons need to face down only and even then the results are not great for any of the utensils we've washed so far. There are many cycles and options, and frankly my wife has basically no idea how to use them. With the user manual only being available online it is highly unlikely she will read it, so now I get to add full time dish loader to the list. Thanks Bosch, not! If I had it to do over, I would have gone to a simpler, cheaper, and louder dishwasher.
